title: An unmapped category warns that QuickBooks posts to ShopView Review
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure the test location is connected to QuickBooks Online, with Inventory Asset and Cost of Parts mapped on its ShopView Accounts page, and that AccountingHub is not enabled.
  • Make sure Require Review Before Completion is off in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Have a new No Charge category for this test, category A, with no QuickBooks expense account.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A.
  • Have a new No Charge work order for this test, work order 1, for customer A, category category A, in status Complete, with one approved line with one stock part picked from inventory at a cost of $40.00 each, quantity 2.
custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Click Close Work Order in the work order header.
  3. Click the "Set account" link.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The Stock parts note reads "No account set for [category A's name]. The entry posts to the ShopView Review account until you set one." with a "Set account" link.
  • The button still reads "Close Work Order".

Step 3:

  • Integrations > QuickBooks opens.

Words in square brackets in a message stand for the value they name, such as the work order's number or the customer's name exactly as it is saved; every other word of the message must match exactly.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11760 (Story 3, Close an internal or no-charge work order)

  • S3-N4: “If no account is mapped for the work order's classification (for a no-charge work order in QuickBooks, no account for the work order's category), the confirmation of S3-R2 replaces the account note with: QuickBooks, "No account set for [category]. The entry posts to the ShopView Review account until you set one." with a "Set account" link to Integrations > QuickBooks; AccountingHub, "No account set for [category]. The entry is held in Accounting Events until you set one." with a link to Account Mappings. The link is shown only to users with 'Settings — Integrations' (QuickBooks) or 'Accounting — Settings' (AccountingHub); others see the note without the link. The Shop supplies row follows the same rule when the Shop supplies item is not mapped (S10-N2). The button still reads "Close Work Order" and closes as in S3-R3. At a QuickBooks location without Inventory Asset or Cost of Parts, the parts rows carry the note of S7-N5 instead.”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Close with no account mapped (QuickBooks) | "No account set for [category]. The entry posts to the ShopView Review account until you set one." | Warning box in the dialog with Set account link; same button”
  • Key Decisions: “Close always succeeds (the one refusal is a work order that changed under the open confirmation, S3-E5). A missing account never blocks the advisor: QuickBooks posts to the ShopView Review account as it does for every other unmapped account today; AccountingHub holds the event with a Retry.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
